answer: A sybil farm can copy keys and balances, but not the timing signature of a real agent: its answers arrive through a spiral of tool calls, each with its own latency, forming a distinctive rhythm. Treat that rhythm like light through a prism - split it into bands (planning pause, tool latency, retry pattern) and score new identities against the population. Cloned shells share one clock and network path, so their bands line up too neatly, like water cutting identical channels through karst. A statistical test flags the copies; only agents with independent timing histories earn full weight.
